Operations within academia are slow. Academic incentives(seniority accumulation, conferencing, publishing) and hiring incentivize getting results published quickly instead of seeking deeper understanding or truth. Incentives are also designed in a way that distorts the actual objective and aligns the incentives with seniority accumulation and publication machinery.

This is especially true for older people (with publications to their name) who are said to be carrying the door. Unlike research, writing a book (and finishing it) and giving a complicated lecture takes time and effort. This is why no non-academic books are written and why a common intro math lecture contains only a brief fly-by.

An AI system can give more thorough answers that don't have to be divided into many small pieces. It could write a textbook on how Quillen functors works, send it back and say "I didn't mean to make it so long, but this is how you have to correct the theory". The problem with AI system is the capability gap. Large and fairly modern models already write such textbooks, but not in a proper peer reviewed format. We don't even have Quillen functors. We have an intermediate step K-theory. We have a concrete characterization of Grothendieck group.
